entities.summary:
Crates of Mallus (b. 200 BCE, Mallus) was a philosopher or thinker of the Classical era, active in Mallus. He was one of the first to explore the relationship between Stoicism and Epicureanism, laying the groundwork for future philosophical debates. His ideas on the nature of the self and the universe had a lasting impact on Western philosophy.

A key figure in the intellectual landscape of ancient Greece, Crates' teachings influenced prominent philosophers such as Epictetus and Seneca. His emphasis on reason, individualism, and the pursuit of happiness resonated with the spirit of the age.

Crates' legacy extends beyond the realm of philosophy, as his ideas about the importance of living in harmony with nature and the interconnectedness of all things influenced the development of ancient Greek art and architecture.

In the words of Epictetus, 'The unexamined life is not worth living,' a phrase that Crates would have undoubtedly agreed with, given his passion for self-reflection and intellectual curiosity.
